body.p: Iwulchan. There was a human. The name of this human was Iwulchan. The human's head was big, without brain. Iwulchan had brothers. Once his wife(?) said to Iwulchan: "Make tent poles!" Iwulchan said: "Fine! I'll make tent poles!" Then Iwulchan took his axe, having taken [it] he chopped down whole trees. He chopped down a whole forest. He was chopping, chopping and chopping. The brothers saw how Iwulchan was chopping down the forest. Having seen they laughed. Then they said to Iwulchan: "Fool! You're chopping whole trees!" Another time the woman said to Iwulchan: "Your brothers hunt wild reindeers, you always sleep! Make a smoke hole in the tent!" Iwulchan said: "Fine! I'll make a smoke hole!" Then Iwulchan climbed onto the tent, he closed the smoke hole. Having closed the smoke hole, he glued up the smoke hole. His wife choked in the tent, she died. The brothers came, having come they said: "Iwulchan, what's up with your wife? Why did she die?" Iwulchan said: "I don't know! I made a smoke hole, my wife died." The brothers said to Iwulchan: "Your wife died. Go to your father-in-law! Ask your father-in-law for clothes!" Iwulchan listened, having listened he said: "I'll go soon! Well, I'll go!" Then he went to the tent of his father-in-law. He reached the father-in-law's tent, having reached he saw a dog. The dog [DCh]: The snuggled up to Iwulchan. Iwulchan killed the dog. "Why did you come?", his father-in-law said.form "alanÄaurÉdÊ¼aÄow" is unclear, really two tense markers? Iwulchan said: "Your daughter died! Give me clothes!" His father-in-law kept the child/children(?). The father-in-law said to Iwulchan: "Keep the child! I'll bring clothes!" Iwulchan said: "Come on! I'll keep the child! You bring clothes for your daughter!" The father-in-law gave the child to Iwulchan and went off. Iwulchan took the child, having taken he pierced the child's head and sucked the brain out. The father-in-law came. Iwulchan said: "Your child has pus in the head. I sucked the pus out, the child fell asleep. One has to heal [it]!" The father-in-law looked at the child, having looked he said: "Why did you kill the child?" Iwulchan said: "I didn't kill, I healed [it]!" So Iwulchan said. Then he took the clothes, he went to his own tent. Iwulchan is coming back, a snowstorm sprang up. The forest made noise and started to sway.[DCh]: The form "muÄugindulaji" is quite unclear.Iwulchan looks and thinks: "This forest is bowing to me. These trees ask me for clothes."[KAY]: Judging by the context there So Iwulchan thought and he tore the clothes. Having torn [it] he hung it in should be plural: 'these trees'pieces on every tree. He hung up all pieces of the clothes in the forest. Iwulchan is coming along his own path. So Iwulchan reached his own tent. The brothers said to Iwulchan: "Did you bring clothes?" Iwulchan said: "No! On the way the forest bowed to me, it asked for clothes, and I gave." The brothers laughed, having laughed the brothers said to Iwulchan: "Now go by boat, hunt fish!" Iwulchan said: "Fine! I'll go along the way (?)! I'll hunt much fish! Well, I'll go!"[DCh]: The sentence does not really make sense from the context. Then Iwulchan went quickly by boat to the ocean. The people saw how Iwulchan was going, they said: "Where are you going, Iwulchan? Go back!" Iwulchan said: "The brothers said me "hunt fish". I hit the road, I'll hunt fish!" So Iwulchan was travelling on. He travelled and travelled. He reached the ocean. At the ocean the old devil woman Huden was sitting. Huden saw Iwulchan, having seen [him] she shouted: "Iwulchan, Iwulchan! Come to me!", the old woman Huden shouted. Iwulchan is looking, he doesn't see anything. "Who shouted at me?", Iwulchan thinks. Then he went to the shore. Here was a big slope. Iwulchan went to the slope. The old devil woman Huden shouted again: "Come to me, Iwulchan! I have a silver comb! I have clothes [made of] sables!" Iwulchan climbed close to the slope, then he sees the woman, the woman cries: "Iwulchan, look back! A wild reindeer is running!" The old devil woman Huden shouted to Iwulchan. Iwulchan looked back, having looked he fell into the water. Iwulchan died. In the third year one human was travelling to the ocean, the name of the human was Barma. Huden saw the human and shouted at him. Barma saw Iwulchan's boat. "Where is Iwulchan?", Barma thinks. "I'll search Iwulchan!" Then Barma climbed up the slope. Here Barma saw the woman, having seen [her] Barma thinks: "I'll catch this woman!" Huden shouted at Barma: "Look back, man! A wild reindeer is running!" Barma said: "What a liar!" Then he ran to the woman, he caught the woman. On the slope there were the three sisters of Huden. Huden was [the] young[est]. Huden said to Barma: "Look what kind of slope [it is]! The slope asks for my sisters' heads". When Huden had uttered these words, the slope crashed, having crashed it squashed Huden and Barma. The sisters found Huden's head, having found they threw it to the slope.
